#### Quick Facts

#### Due Date

**Final exam period, December 7-10, 2026 (exact slot TBD)**

#### Where this fits

This is the last step: revise your whole paper. The [poster](project-poster.qmd) is turned in separately and presents the same four sections. See the [project overview](project-overview.qmd) for the full roadmap.

#### Goal

The goal of the final edited project is to turn your draft into a cohesive research paper (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) analyzing your collected Islands data.

#### To Turn In

- In your RStudio Project folder, go back to `islands-paper.qmd` and make any changes or additions based on feedback you received.
- Upload both your `islands-paper.qmd` and the rendered PDF (`islands-paper.pdf`) to Canvas. Every checkpoint requires both files.
- Personal reflection as a PDF file submitted to Canvas. Everyone submits their own, even if you worked in a group.
:::


## Assignment Deliverables

See [project-draft.qmd](project-draft.qmd) for details on the submission of the complete draft of your Islands research project combining all prior components into a unified, publication-style report.

## Reflection

Submit a personal reflection:

- **Personal Reflection (1–2 pages):**  
  Describe what you learned from the Islands Project.  
  Address questions such as:
  - Which parts were most enjoyable or most challenging?  
  - Which parts connected most to class material?  
  - Which skills transfer to other contexts?  
  - What statistical ideas do you want to explore further?
